clue.text: Chorister apt to be confused if found here

definitions.text: Chorister apt to be confused if found here

indicators.note: letters that are confused get muddled up, so the two words chorister and apt are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A choirboy who might easily lose his way if placed in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of CHORISTER APT rearrange into the answer, and a singer placed among the instrumentalists below the stage could well be confused.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunken area in front of a stage where the musicians play is the place a chorister would feel out of place.

clue.text: Reserve lovely skirts for regular

parts.note: to reserve something, such as a book or a meal, is to order it

indicators.note: the skirts of something are its edges, so take the outside letters of lovely

explanation.surface: Someone books a pretty skirt to wear for a regular customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things arranged neatly and methodically, following a steady pattern.

clue.text: Young animals left out in holes in the ground

indicators.note: left out says the letter for left is removed from the young animals

parts.note: the young of cattle are calves

explanation.surface: Baby animals abandoned in burrows in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like a description of abandoned animals, but it tells you to remove L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollow chambers in rock or earth are natural holes in the ground.

clue.text: Twice, say, accepting Republican promises of payment — very bad

indicators.note: accepting means the doubled pair takes the Republican letter inside it
twice asks for the example abbreviation to be written two times in a row

parts.note: say introduces an example, the abbreviation e.g.
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A Republican politician keeps signing IOUs, and it is all going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts R inside EGEG, giving EGREG, before IOUS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flagrantly or shockingly bad is described with this word, as in an outrageous mistake.

clue.text: Taunt Dickens character wanting seconds

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter for seconds is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the title hero of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A jibe at Oliver Twist, who famously asked for more food.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Oliver asking for more: 'wanting seconds' looks like hunger but removes S.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease or ridicule someone, especially for a mistake, is a verb sense of this word.

clue.text: I got scan to be reviewed, being sceptical

indicators.note: something reviewed is gone over again and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient wants a medical scan checked again, doubting the results.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who doubts that God's existence can be known holds a sceptical position on religion.

clue.text: State "I date a prostitute"

parts.note: ho is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A shameless confession that the speaker is seeing a sex worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb introducing the quoted words, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty United States, in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: E. coli's in stew, which might be cause of bust-up?

definitions.text: which might be cause of bust-up?

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture of things cooked together, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A food-poisoning bacterium in a casserole, which could start a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust-up' looks like a quarrel, but the definition plays on breast enlargement: implants of this material push the bust up.
explanation.definitionFit: Breast implants are often made of this synthetic polymer, so it can literally cause a bust to rise.

clue.text: Nevertheless, how Bill ran America from 1993 to 2001

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned word for nonetheless or all the same

definitions.text: how Bill ran America from 1993 to 2001
definitions.meaning: Bill Clinton was president ... Gore as his vice-president, so he governed alongside Al

explanation.surface: A fact about the Clinton presidency, prefaced by a grudging concession.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as WITH AL: Bill Clinton ran the country with Al Gore as his deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adverb means notwithstanding or all the same, and also besides.

clue.text: American loon going to Swiss town provides amusement

parts.note: the bird Americans call a loon is called a diver in Britain
Sion is a town in the Swiss canton of Valais

explanation.surface: A bird watcher's trip to Switzerland to see a loon proves entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loon' suggests a crazy person, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertaining pastime that takes the mind off other things is a pleasant distraction.

clue.text: Story of a large wading bird with no tail

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: with no tail means the final letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: the ibis is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A tall tale about a big bird that has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse offered to show you were elsewhere is a story told to escape blame.

clue.text: Quit, or extend contract?

definitions.meaning: to quit is to give up a post or job
to put your name to the contract once more, renewing it

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is RE-SIGN, sign again; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a job formally is stepping down, while signing a fresh deal is putting pen to paper again.

clue.text: Surprise! Part of Birmingham is hot

parts.note: Aston is a district of Birmingham, home of Aston Villa football club
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An announcement that one Birmingham neighbourhood is having a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston is an inner-city district of Birmingham, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze or stun someone is to take them greatly by surprise.

clue.text: Concern about consuming a flowering plant

indicators.note: consuming means the turned word takes the a inside it
about means the word for concern is turned round

parts.note: worry is anxiety or concern

explanation.surface: Anxiety over eating a flower that might be poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns WORRY into YRROW; 'consuming' then puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Achillea, a hedgerow plant with flat white flower heads, is known by this common name.

clue.text: To undergo a second period of abstinence is evocative

parts.note: to do something a second time is to redo it
Lent is the forty days before Easter when Christians give things up

explanation.surface: Someone facing a second stint of going without finds it brings back memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent or scene reminiscent of something calls it vividly to mind, which is what evocative means.

clue.text: Good candidate for job involving late work with long shifts

definitions.text: Good candidate for job involving late work

indicators.note: shifts means moves about, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruiter's description of the ideal applicant for a demanding night-time role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like part of the job description of long working hours, but it signals rearranging WITH LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who habitually stays awake and active until late suits work done after dark.

clue.text: Listen to a fight on the radio in the general vicinity

indicators.note: on the radio means the words are heard rather than seen, so their sound is what counts

parts.note: to listen to something is to hear it; a gives A; a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: Tuning in to a boxing match broadcast on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning near this place or somewhere around here, describing a general location.

clue.text: Reprehensible row in back of court

parts.note: base means morally low or reprehensible
a line is a row, as of people or seats

explanation.surface: A shameful quarrel breaks out at the rear of a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' and 'court' suggest a legal dispute; the court is a tennis court and 'row' is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the line marking the far end of the court is at the back of it.

clue.text: Millipede's talent is protecting foot

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as if guarding it within

explanation.surface: A many-legged creature's gift shields its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks like part of the millipede, but it is the definition: the base of a column or statue.
explanation.definitionFit: The base on which a statue or column stands is its foot or support.

clue.text: Poke fun at staff without wages? On the contrary

indicators.note: without means outside, so one word goes round the other
on the contrary says the order is the other way about, so the wages go outside the staff

parts.note: pay means wages
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Mocking employees who go unpaid, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'staff without wages' puts the staff outside; 'On the contrary' reverses the roles, so the wages go round the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock something by imitating it in an exaggerated way is to make fun of it.

clue.text: Jolly spiffing run, heading west into light wind

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftwards, so the letter for run travels left into the middle of the slang word

parts.note: beezer is old British schoolboy slang for excellent, like spiffing
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An upper-class exclamation of delight on a run into a gentle wind.
explanation.walkthrough: BEEZER and spiffing are dated British slang for first-rate; the R at its end moves left to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle, pleasant wind is the sense of this word, as in a sea breeze.

clue.text: Waxes former girlfriend, quietly and slowly at first

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of slowly is used

explanation.surface: An ex-partner having a quiet, unhurried waxing session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waxes' looks like hair removal, but it means grows, as the moon waxes.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon waxes it grows larger, and this verb means swells or grows.

clue.text: Fancied mum in lounge, wearing red

indicators.note: the colour word is worn around the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means the silencing letters go inside the word for lounge

parts.note: to lounge is to lie about
mum as in keep mum means silence, given as sh

explanation.surface: Someone took a liking to their mother lying in a red outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but the call for silence, as in keep mum; 'in' and 'wearing' are both container signals, the colour wrapping the rest, which makes LISHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fancied something is to have enjoyed or liked it greatly.

clue.text: Reportedly drives away in people carriers?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we want a word sounding like the word for drives away

parts.note: to shoo is to drive animals or people away

explanation.surface: A news story about motorists heading off in their minivans.
explanation.walkthrough: A people carrier is a British term for a minivan; the question mark signals that the footwear carries people on foot instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear carries people about, so the people carriers of the clue are what we walk in.

clue.text: Knock supporting structure over with power

parts.note: a wall is a structure that holds up a building
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Knocking a load-bearing wall down with power tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy blow or thump is a knock, and this word means one.

clue.text: Dance down under?

parts.note: a dance where the dancer leans backwards and goes low beneath a bar, not one from Australia

explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia, but the dancer goes down and under a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean dance has performers bending backwards to pass beneath a lowered pole.

clue.text: Drunk around start of lunch time

indicators.note: around means the drunk goes round the next letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of lunch is used

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering about from the beginning of lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotted period in a schedule, such as a time slot for a meeting.

clue.text: Wild dog fending off bears

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the phrase carries the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A feral dog fighting off bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals, but it means carries.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild dog native to Australia is known by this name.

clue.text: The proof that John Donne was wrong?

definitions.text: The proof that John Donne was wrong?

parts.words: The proof that John Donne was wrong?
parts.note: Donne wrote that no man is an island, so a place that is an island for a man would contradict him

explanation.walkthrough: John Donne, the 17th-century poet, wrote 'No man is an island'; this Irish Sea island, a British Crown dependency, has a name that seems to refute him.
explanation.definitionFit: The island between Britain and Ireland has a name that reads as an island belonging to a man.

clue.text: Extravagant, very large marquee, say, at Oxford University is overwhelming

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a marquee is an example of a large tent

indicators.note: overwhelming means the word is engulfs the university's letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An enormous marquee at an Oxford college event is simply too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelming' looks like an adjective describing the marquee, but it is a container signal acting on 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and designed to impress, the answer describes lavish display.
